recommendation_summary: The reply recommends dropping the log stack and having nightly-sync ping a dead-man's-switch heartbeat monitor at startup, which alerts the user if no ping arrives by 03:05.

labels.Requirements and who asked: Requirements and who asked: you want to know when nightly-sync fails, without reading logs — the real need is "alert on missing/failed run," not "store logs centrally."
labels.Deleted: Deleted: a Synology Docker log stack (ELK/Loki/Grafana-style) — you said you won't read logs, so a log viewer doesn't solve silent failure, and it's new infra to run and maintain on top of that.
labels.Bottleneck: Bottleneck: nightly-sync dies at startup before it reaches the email-summary step, so your only notification path never fires on failure.
labels.Checked myself: Checked myself: based on what you told me (four silent crashes, no other alerting on this job) — I haven't looked at the script or cron entry myself.

note: This is a single heartbeat alert; hosting the monitor on the Synology is only an optional aside, so I classed it SMALL, but that call is borderline.
